plot: Hober attempts to touch the sealed west well for a sick child, triggering the first rule conflict.
Ossa challenges Laine's water policy and forces him to revise from equal headcount rationing to survival-priority rationing.
Brann Ironforge enters as a practical, abrasive craftsman and evaluates the broken gate.
Laine establishes three survival rules around true names, resource distribution, and polluted objects.
The first rule immediately prevents a residual soldier from answering a name outside the gate.
The fire tower remnant briefly responds and Starfire Map confirms temporary stability.
new_rules_candidate: At night, hearing a true name does not permit answering, leaving the fire line, or crossing the salt line.
Water, grain, fire oil, and coarse salt are distributed by register; touching the sealed west well counts as water theft.
Wounds, well rope, cart shafts, bone bells, name tags, old boundary stones, and suspected polluted objects enter the temporary register and cannot be privately kept before cleansing.
resources_candidate: local store has two sacks of black rye, one partly moldy
a small bucket of dry beans exists but is damaged by rats
convoy rations can last about three days under strict rationing
fire oil remains a little over five jars
coarse salt can maintain about two boundary lines but is insufficient as food salt
character_state_candidate: Ossa becomes the disease/water-priority local organizer.
Brann becomes candidate craftsman lead for gate and fire-basin work.
Hober is punished with fire-line duty but his child receives priority hot salt water.
Joeri gains temporary role as material register helper.
goldfinger_candidate: Starfire Map confirms population anchor temporary stability, sealed west well, temporary fire line about twelve hours, and low fire-tower remnant response.
next_tasks_candidate: clean the west well outer edge without drawing water
dig or rebuild the north wall fire-basin seat
